enriched.title: Present Perfect e Vocabulário do Dia a Dia
enriched.summary: A aula aborda o uso do tempo verbal Present Perfect e inclui vocabulário relacionado a mudanças ou eventos recentes. Além disso, há foco em pronúncia e prática com frases de exemplo.

vocabulary.definition: To separate into pieces as a result of a blow, shock, or strain.
examples: The glass broke when it fell.

vocabulary.definition: The money paid for a journey on public transportation.
examples: The bus fare has gone up.
He couldn't afford the train fare.
Regular practice will improve your skills.

vocabulary.definition: To increase in size, number, or importance.

examples: We arrived at the station on time.

vocabulary.definition: To move downward, typically rapidly and freely without control.
examples: Leaves fall from trees in autumn.

grammar.explanation: The Present Perfect is used to describe actions or events that have occurred at an unspecified time in the past and are relevant to the present.
rules: Used to talk about experiences, changes, or actions with ongoing relevance.
examples: The bus fare has gone up.
commonMistakes: Using the Simple Past instead of Present Perfect (e.g., 'Lisa broke her leg' instead of 'Lisa has broken her leg').
Forgetting to use 'has' or 'have' (e.g., 'Lisa broken her leg' instead of 'Lisa has broken her leg').

practiceQuestions.question: Complete the sentence: Lisa _______ her leg.
practiceQuestions.explanation: The Present Perfect is used to describe an action that happened in the past but has relevance to the present.

practiceQuestions.question: Choose the correct form: The temperature (has fallen/fell) recently.
practiceQuestions.explanation: The Present Perfect is used to talk about recent changes or events.

culturalNotes: In English-speaking countries, being able to discuss changes, such as weather or personal updates, is a common part of casual conversation.
The Present Perfect is often used in British English to describe recent events, while in American English, the Simple Past is more common in these contexts.
studyTips: Practice forming sentences in the Present Perfect using your own experiences or daily observations.
Listen to native speakers using the Present Perfect in context, such as in news reports or interviews.
Review irregular verb forms regularly to ensure you use the correct past participle.
originalExamples: Lisa has broken her leg. (Lisa quebrou a perna.)
The bus fare has gone up. (A tarifa de ônibus aumentou.)
Her English has improved. (O inglês dela melhorou.)
Dan has grown a beard. (Dan deixou a barba crescer.)
The letter has arrived. (A carta chegou.)
The temperature has fallen. (A temperatura caiu.)
